items.en: With what kind of water is Julius washed first?
items.hint: an adjective in the ablative agreeing with aquā (ablative of means)

items.en: Which guests arrive at Julius' house?
items.hint: the nominative subjects of adveniunt; the wives are in an ablative phrase with cum

items.en: Why do the guests come expected today?
items.hint: a nam clause with the perfect; ad cēnam = 'to dinner'

items.en: At what hour do the Romans take dinner?
items.hint: an ablative of time when with ordinal numbers

items.en: Is Julius glad that the guests are present?
items.hint: a yes/no question with -ne; gaudeō takes an indirect statement (vōs adesse)

items.q: Cūr Cornēlius prius urbem relinquere nōn potuit?
items.en: Why couldn't Cornelius leave the city earlier?
items.hint: prae + ablative giving the cause ('because of')

items.q: Quandō Orontēs ex itinere Rōmam revertit?
items.en: When did Orontes return to Rome from his journey?
items.hint: an ablative of time when (Īdibus Māiīs = on the Ides of May)

items.en: From where does Orontes come today?
items.hint: a city name in the ablative for place from which (no preposition); unde in the sentence = 'from where'

items.en: What does Julius diligently see to?
items.hint: cūrō ut + present subjunctive; praesum takes the dative (agricolīs)

items.q: Num Orontēs umquam īnstrūmentō rūsticō ūsus est?
items.en: Orontes has never used a farm tool, has he?
items.hint: num expects 'no'; ūtor is deponent and takes the ablative (ūsus est = has used)

items.q: Quot hōrae iam sunt cum Iūlius cibum nōn sūmpsit?
items.en: How many hours is it now since Julius last ate?
items.hint: a numeral with hōrae in the nominative; cum + perfect here = 'since'

items.en: What does Julius doubt?
items.hint: dubitō num + present subjunctive (an indirect question: 'whether')

items.q: Utrum molestius est, famēs an sitis?
items.en: Which is more troublesome, hunger or thirst?
items.hint: utrum … an; a nominative with the comparative molestior (multō = 'by much')

items.q: Quid Cornēlius māvult quam sitim patī?
items.en: What does Cornelius prefer to suffering thirst?
items.hint: mālō + infinitive … quam + infinitive

items.q: Quā rē Orontēs cotīdiē fruī vult?
items.en: What does Orontes want to enjoy every day?
items.hint: fruor (deponent) takes the ablative

items.en: Why do we drink, according to Cornelius?
items.hint: a purpose clause: ut + present subjunctive

items.q: Quis cibum coquit atque cēnam in culīnā parat?
items.en: Who cooks the food and prepares dinner in the kitchen?
items.hint: the nominative predicate with appellātur; cuius is a genitive relative ('whose')

items.en: How many couches are there in the dining room?
items.hint: a numeral in the nominative plural

items.en: How do the Romans dine?
items.hint: a present participle in the nominative plural (cubantēs = reclining)

items.en: When will the guests dine?
items.hint: cum prīmum + future perfect (parāverit, ōrnāverint) after a future main verb

items.en: What does the boy finally announce?
items.hint: an indirect statement with a perfect passive infinitive (parātam esse)

items.en: Where does Julius recline with Aemilia?
items.hint: in + ablative for place where

items.en: What is the main course?
items.hint: the nominative subject after the colon, with a relative clause (quem … ēlēgit)

items.en: With what does the attendant cut the pork?
items.hint: an ablative of instrument; convīvīs spectantibus is an ablative absolute

items.q: Cūr Orontēs cibum suum sale aspergit?
items.en: Why does Orontes sprinkle salt on his food?
items.hint: a purpose clause: ut + present subjunctive; sale is an ablative of means

items.en: Who alone drinks unmixed wine?
items.hint: the nominative subject; cui is a dative with placet

items.q: Ex quō vīnum Iūliī factum est?
items.en: From what was Julius' wine made?
items.hint: ex + ablative for the material

items.q: Quāle est vīnum Iūliī, ut Paula dīcit?
items.en: What is Julius' wine like, according to Paula?
items.hint: a predicate adjective agreeing with the neuter vīnum

items.en: What does Paula always mix into her wine?
items.hint: the accusative object of misceō; vīnō is a dative ('with wine')

items.en: When will Orontes give his opinion?
items.hint: nōn ante … quam + future perfect (gustāverit); utrumque = 'both of the two'

items.q: Utrum vīnum melius esse omnēs sentiunt?
items.en: Which wine do all feel is better?
items.hint: an indirect statement; vīnō Albānō is an ablative of comparison after melius

items.en: Which of the two dares to speak openly?
items.hint: neuter = 'neither of the two'; eōrum is a partitive genitive
